data.name: Roopa
data.long_meaning: Roopa is a Sanskrit word derived from the root 'Rup' meaning form or appearance. In Hindu mythology, Roopa is the divine manifestation of Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity and beauty. She is also known as 'Sri Roopa' and is often depicted as a beautiful woman with golden complexion, four arms, and holding lotus flowers and a golden lotus. Roopa symbolizes the divine beauty and grace that adorns the universe and bestows prosperity and happiness.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine beauty and grace.
data.numerology_meaning: Roopa is a nurturing and loving name that resonates with the energy of harmony, balance, and beauty.

data.spiritual_significance: According to Hindu beliefs, the name Roopa has a deep spiritual significance as it represents the divine grace and beauty of the Goddess Lakshmi. Those named Roopa are believed to possess inner and outer beauty, grace, and fortunes. It is said that invoking the name of Roopa brings blessings of prosperity, happiness, and good fortune.

historical_references.reference: Roopa was a name of a queen consort in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. She was the wife of King Yudhishthira and is also known as Draupadi. She was taken as a common wife by the five Pandava brothers after they won her in a swayamvara (self-chosen) contest.

Roopa was a goddess in Hinduism, particularly revered in Eastern India. She is considered a form of the goddess Saraswati and is associated with knowledge, wisdom, and learning. Her iconography includes a white elephant, a book, and a lotus.
